title: A Ni(OH)2 symmetric battery cell for hydroxide exchange membrane-based direct air capture of CO2 - Nature Energy
text:
AbstractElectrochemical carbon capture is a promising low-energy-cost solution for direct air capture (DAC) by using renewable electricity and avoiding traditional, energy intensive thermal swing sorption. While several electrochemical devices have been proposed, few have achieved promised low energy costs while maintaining high durability and full purification of CO2; moreover, scale-up and pressure drop are rarely considered for these devices. Here we show a symmetric nickel hydroxide battery design with a hydroxide exchange membrane durably tested in a laboratory-sized 25-cm2 device for 5,000 h. Over a 48-h test, a scaled-up 9 × 300 cm2 electrochemical stack achieved an energy cost of 132 kJ molCO2−1 and flux of 0.19 molCO2 m−2 h−1 equivalent to 0.83 MWh tCO2−1 and 75 kgCO2 m2 yr−1. In addition, the pilot-scale stack meets the 300 Pa pressure drop requirements for DAC. A pathway to below US$100 tCO2−1 is presented on the basis of energy technology learning rates, showcasing electrochemical DAC as a potential climate change solution.
